saints.name: St. Nicholas of Flüe
saints.title: Hermit
saints.shortBlurb: A Swiss farmer, soldier, and magistrate who, with his wife's consent, became a hermit and peacemaker of the Confederation…
biography: Born in 1417 at Flüeli near Sachseln in Unterwalden, Nicholas was a farmer who fought as a soldier at Ragaz in 1446, rose to captain, and served his canton as councillor and judge, declining the office of Landammann. With his wife Dorothea he had ten children.

In 1467, past fifty and with Dorothea's consent, he left his household for a hermitage in the nearby Ranft gorge, moved by a vision of a lily devoured by a horse, which he read as the world's cares swallowing up the spirit. There for some twenty years he gave himself to prayer and penance, said to have taken no earthly food but the Eucharist.

His counsel was sought from across Europe, and in 1481 his intervention at the Diet of Stans reconciled the quarreling cantons and saved the Confederation from civil war. He died on 21 March 1487, surrounded by his wife and children, and was canonized by Pius XII in 1947 — the peacemaker who is honoured as patron of Switzerland.
saints.knownFor: His hidden life of prayer and his peacemaking at Stans.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 21 March
